narrative: Your promotion was denied because the model flagged you as an exit risk, estimating a 48% probability that you will leave—high enough in this process to treat you as likely to depart. The strongest driver was that you reported having other job opportunities; only about a quarter of employees predicted to stay had such offers, so this pushed the result strongly toward leaving. The next most important factor was your six to ten years in your current organization, which pulled toward staying and is common among stayers. Your six to ten years of total experience ranked third and pushed slightly toward leaving. Other context—no bonus, no medical insurance, low job support, no recognition, no useful training, and not feeling you received the deserved promotion—reinforces the exit-risk signal. This is not a final judgment about you; it is a prompt for a retention conversation. The organization should clarify promotion criteria, review recognition, support, training and benefits, and ask what would keep you. You should discuss your external opportunities and the conditions—career path, recognition and support—that would make staying worthwhile.
